s1.syndrome_frame: Acute heart failure with signs of volume overload and possible restrictive cardiomyopathy
salient_findings: New-onset heart failure symptoms 2 weeks after COVID-19 vaccination booster
Signs of volume overload with lower-extremity edema and jugular venous distention
Elevated N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide and abnormal echocardiogram findings
key_facts: 59-year-old man with history of hypertension and medication-induced diabetes
Symptoms began 2 weeks after receiving COVID-19 vaccination booster
No significant family history
Past medical conditions include hypertension and medication-induced diabetes
Blood urea nitrogen: 46 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.79 mg/dL
Uric acid: 14.1 mg/dL
N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide: 206 ng/dL
Negative results for tuberculin skin testing, rheumatoid factor, antinuclear antibody, and viral studies
Electrocardiogram showed PR depressions and inferolateral ST-segment elevation
Echocardiogram revealed left ventricular ejection fraction: 64%, right ventricular dysfunction, and increased inferior vena cava size

shortlist.label: Constrictive pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Thickened pericardium and evidence of ventricular interdependence on cardiac MRI

shortlist.label: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Right ventricular dysfunction and increased inferior vena cava size on echocardiogram

shortlist.label: COVID-19 vaccine-associated myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Symptoms began 2 weeks after receiving COVID-19 vaccination booster

shortlist.label: Post-myocarditic restrictive cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide and recent COVID-19 vaccination

shortlist.label: Amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Restrictive cardiomyopathy and possible systemic involvement suggested by uric acid and creatinine levels

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging studies, including thickened pericardium on cardiac MRI and evidence of ventricular interdependence and septal bounce, are consistent with constrictive pericarditis. The elevated N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide and signs of volume overload also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While restrictive cardiomyopathy could explain some of the patient's symptoms, the imaging studies and cardiac catheterization results are more consistent with constrictive pericarditis.

rejected.label: COVID-19 vaccine-associated myocarditis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms began 2 weeks after receiving the COVID-19 vaccination booster, but the imaging studies and laboratory results do not support myocarditis as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Post-myocarditic restrictive cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of prior myocarditis, and the patient's symptoms and imaging studies are more consistent with constrictive pericarditis.

rejected.label: Amyloidosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of amyloidosis in the patient's laboratory results or imaging studies, and the clinical presentation is not typical for amyloidosis.
